title: EviGraph: Towards Verifiable Evidence Construction for Information-Seeking Agents

visual_explainer.question: How can an information-seeking agent turn retrieved pages into auditable claim-level state while separating retrieval, recording, and stopping failures?
visual_explainer.takeaway: A frozen verifier extracts span-grounded evidence, a shared policy proposes graph writes, and a structural validator commits only provenance-valid updates; the graph then drives search and process rewards.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same dual-role architecture without RL, plus a monolithic search agent under the same BrowseComp-Plus interaction budget.

analysis.tldr: EviGraph materializes search evidence as a span-grounded claim graph and trains search plus graph-writing roles with process rewards. On BrowseComp-Plus, the clean same-architecture comparison is 26.9% without RL versus 35.9% with RL. The much larger 2.7→26.9 jump also changes architecture, verifier access, search persistence, and stopping, so it is package evidence rather than a graph-memory effect.
analysis.problem: A search trace can contain relevant pages without proving which source span supports which candidate constraint, making grounding, contradiction, and stopping difficult to supervise independently.
analysis.core_idea: Separate executor search, frozen page verification, policy-proposed evidence recording, and deterministic structural validation around a persistent claim–evidence graph that exposes positive support, conflicts, and missing constraints.
analysis.agent_loop: question/constraints → graph-conditioned search → frozen page verification → Add/Support proposal → structural commit → updated support/conflict/MISSING state → continue or answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The executor never sees raw pages; a frozen verifier inspects results and returns source-anchored spans. The graph controls subsequent querying and stopping, while retrieval failure, recording failure, and decision failure become distinct transitions.
compared_to: cross-benchmark BrowseComp, GAIA, XBench and LiveVQA transfer
analysis.evidence: BrowseComp-Plus accuracy is 35.9% for Qwen3-8B EviGraph with RL versus 26.9% for the same dual-role architecture without RL and 2.7% for the monolithic agent. The RL comparison keeps the architecture and interaction budget aligned and does not gain by simply increasing search volume.
analysis.why_it_matters: It moves evidence materialization from an opaque trajectory into explicit mutable state and gives a sharper causal vocabulary for retrieval, recording, contradiction handling, and stopping.
limitations: The 2.7→26.9 package gain changes role decomposition, raw-page access, verifier mediation, search persistence, and stopping together.
The frozen verifier supplies privileged semantic judgments; the deterministic validator guarantees structure and provenance, not truth or entailment.
Reported generated-token accounting excludes environment-supplied page text and does not provide complete wall-clock or dollar accounting.
The strongest controlled evidence isolates the RL objective only within the authors' dual-role architecture.
